title: Geography: India, North-East and the World
why: Geography gives 5–7 of the 50 GK questions in the IPO paper, and they are pure recall: which country a volcano or island is in, which country holds the largest oil reserve, which river/pass/park belongs where. The 2022 paper asked Mount Agung, Lord Howe Island and Venezuela's oil reserves — all table facts. Learn the tables here and these become 10-second marks.

lessons.title: India: location, extent, borders and states
lessons.body:
### Location and size — the numbers examiners love

| Item | Fact |
|---|---|
| Latitudinal extent (mainland) | 8°4′N to 37°6′N |
| Longitudinal extent | 68°7′E to 97°25′E |
| N–S length / E–W width | ~3,214 km / ~2,933 km |
| Area | ~3.287 million sq km = ~2.4% of world land; **7th largest** country |
| Standard meridian (IST) | **82°30′E**, passes near **Mirzapur (UP)**; IST = GMT + 5:30 |
| States the standard meridian crosses | UP, MP, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, Andhra Pradesh |
| Tropic of Cancer (23°30′N) crosses 8 states | **Gujarat, Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura, Mizoram** |
| Southernmost point | **Indira Point** (Great Nicobar); mainland: Kanyakumari (Cape Comorin) |
| Easternmost / westernmost | Kibithu (Arunachal) / Guhar Moti (Kutch, Gujarat) |
| Land frontier | ~15,200 km |
| Coastline | Old figure **7,516.6 km**; re-measured at **11,098.81 km** (GIS re-measurement by the National Hydrographic Office & Survey of India, 2023–24; notified by the Ports & Shipping Ministry, 29 Apr 2025). Gujarat has the longest state coastline (~2,340 km); A&N Islands the longest of any state/UT |

> Memory hook for the Tropic of Cancer: **"Gu-Ra-M-Ch-J-W-T-M"** — go west to east: Gujarat → Rajasthan → MP → Chhattisgarh → Jharkhand → West Bengal → Tripura → Mizoram. Odisha, Bihar, Assam and Meghalaya are the usual wrong options.

### Neighbours and land borders (longest first)

| Country | Approx. border (km) | Indian states/UTs touching it |
|---|---|---|
| **Bangladesh** | 4,096 (longest) | West Bengal (longest share), Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram |
| China | 3,488 | Ladakh, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Sikkim, Arunachal Pradesh |
| Pakistan | 3,323 | Gujarat, Rajasthan, Punjab, J&K, Ladakh |
| Nepal | 1,751 | Uttarakhand, UP, Bihar, West Bengal, Sikkim |
| Myanmar | 1,643 | Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram |
| Bhutan | 699 | Sikkim, West Bengal, Assam, Arunachal Pradesh |
| Afghanistan | 106 (shortest) | Ladakh (via PoK/Gilgit-Baltistan, claimed) |

- Sri Lanka is separated by the **Palk Strait** and Gulf of Mannar; **Adam's Bridge (Ram Setu)** is the shoal chain between Pamban (Rameswaram) and Mannar.
- Maldives lies south of Lakshadweep across the **Eight Degree Channel**.

### States and UTs (as of September 2026: 28 states, 8 UTs)

| Superlative | Answer |
|---|---|
| Largest state by area | **Rajasthan** (then MP, Maharashtra) |
| Smallest state by area | **Goa** |
| Most populous state | Uttar Pradesh |
| Largest UT by area | Ladakh; smallest UT: Lakshadweep |
| Newest UTs (as of Sept 2026) | J&K and Ladakh (31 Oct 2019); Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu merged (26 Jan 2020) |
| Siliguri Corridor ("Chicken's Neck") | ~20–22 km wide strip in West Bengal linking the North-East to the rest of India |

lessons.title: Relief: Himalaya, peninsular ranges, peaks and passes
lessons.body:
### Physiographic divisions (NCERT)
1. **Himalayan mountains** (young fold mountains)
2. **Northern plains** (Indo-Gangetic-Brahmaputra alluvium)
3. **Peninsular plateau** (oldest, Gondwana block — Deccan, Malwa, Chotanagpur, Meghalaya/Shillong plateau)
4. **Indian desert** (Thar)
5. **Coastal plains** (western: Konkan, Kanara, Malabar; eastern: Utkal, Andhra, Coromandel)
6. **Islands** (Andaman & Nicobar — tertiary mountains; Lakshadweep — coral)

### Three parallel ranges of the Himalaya

| Range | Also called | Key features |
|---|---|---|
| Greater Himalaya | **Himadri** | Highest, avg ~6,000 m, perennially snow-bound; granite core |
| Lesser Himalaya | **Himachal** | Pir Panjal, Dhauladhar, Mahabharat ranges; hill stations (Shimla, Mussoorie, Nainital, Darjeeling); Kashmir & Kangra valleys |
| Outer Himalaya | **Shiwaliks** | Lowest; longitudinal valleys called **duns** (Dehradun) |
| Trans-Himalaya | — | Karakoram, Ladakh, Zaskar ranges |
| Purvanchal | Eastern hills | Patkai Bum, Naga hills, Manipur hills, Mizo (Lushai) hills |

### Highest peaks

| Peak | Height (m) | Where |
|---|---|---|
| K2 (Godwin Austen) | 8,611 | Karakoram; in PoK/Gilgit-Baltistan (claimed by India) |
| **Kangchenjunga** | 8,586 | Sikkim–Nepal border; highest peak in India (Indian-administered) |
| **Nanda Devi** | 7,816 | Uttarakhand; highest peak **entirely within** India |
| Kamet | 7,756 | Uttarakhand |
| Kangto | ~7,060 | Arunachal Pradesh (highest in Arunachal) |
| **Anamudi** | 2,695 | Kerala; highest in Western Ghats / South India |
| Doddabetta | 2,637 | Nilgiris (Tamil Nadu) |
| Jindhagada | 1,690 | Highest in Eastern Ghats (Andhra Pradesh) |
| **Guru Shikhar** | 1,722 | Mount Abu; highest in the **Aravallis** (oldest fold mountains of India) |
| Dhupgarh | 1,350 | Pachmarhi; highest in the Satpuras |
| Saddle Peak | 732 | North Andaman; highest in A&N |

- **Mount Everest** (Sagarmatha / Chomolungma) is in Nepal–China; official height **8,848.86 m** (Nepal–China joint measurement, 2020).
- **Nilgiris** are where the Eastern and Western Ghats meet.

### Mountain passes (very frequently asked)

| Pass | State/UT | Connects / notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Zoji La** | J&K–Ladakh | Srinagar – Leh (Zojila tunnel under construction) |
| **Banihal** | J&K | Jammu – Srinagar; **Jawahar Tunnel** |
| Khardung La | Ladakh | Leh – Nubra/Shyok valley; among highest motorable passes |
| Karakoram Pass | Ladakh | Ladakh – Xinjiang (China) |
| **Shipki La** | Himachal | Sutlej enters India; trade route to Tibet |
| **Rohtang** | Himachal | Manali (Kullu) – Lahaul-Spiti; **Atal Tunnel** (2020) bypasses it |
| Baralacha La | Himachal | On Manali – Leh road |
| **Lipulekh** | Uttarakhand | India–Nepal–China trijunction; Kailash-Mansarovar route |
| Mana, Niti | Uttarakhand | To Tibet |
| **Nathu La** | Sikkim | Gangtok – Lhasa; border trade & Kailash yatra route |
| Jelep La | Sikkim | Sikkim – Chumbi valley (Tibet) |
| Bomdi La, **Sela** | Arunachal | Route to Tawang; Sela tunnel (2024) |
| Diphu | Arunachal | India–Myanmar–China trijunction |
| **Pangsau** | Arunachal | India – Myanmar; old Stilwell (Ledo) Road |
| **Palghat (Palakkad) Gap** | Kerala–Tamil Nadu | Break in Western Ghats between Nilgiri and Anaimalai hills |
| **Thal Ghat / Bhor Ghat** | Maharashtra | Nashik–Mumbai / Pune–Mumbai through the Sahyadri |

> Hook: **La** means "pass" in Tibetan — Zoji La, Nathu La, Shipki La. Tunnels: **Jawahar = Banihal**, **Atal = Rohtang**.

lessons.title: Rivers, lakes, waterfalls and dams
lessons.body:
### Himalayan river systems

| River | Source | Key facts |
|---|---|---|
| **Indus** | Near Mansarovar (Tibet) | Enters India in Ladakh; tributaries Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, Sutlej. Indus Waters Treaty 1960 (World Bank-brokered): eastern rivers (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej) to India, western (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab) to Pakistan |
| Jhelum | Verinag spring (Kashmir) | Flows through **Wular Lake** and Srinagar |
| Chenab | Chandra + Bhaga meet at Tandi (HP) | Largest Indus tributary by volume; Salal, Baglihar dams; Chenab rail bridge |
| Sutlej | Rakshastal (Tibet) | Enters via **Shipki La**; **Bhakra** dam; Beas joins it at Harike |
| **Ganga** | **Bhagirathi** (Gangotri, Gaumukh) + **Alaknanda** meet at **Devprayag** | ~2,525 km — longest river of India; National River (2008); Padma in Bangladesh |
| Yamuna | Yamunotri glacier | Longest tributary of Ganga; joins at Prayagraj (Triveni Sangam); tributaries Chambal, Betwa, Ken |
| Son | Amarkantak | Major right-bank tributary of Ganga |
| Kosi | Nepal Himalaya | **"Sorrow of Bihar"** (shifts course) |
| Damodar | Chotanagpur plateau | **"Sorrow of Bengal"**; Damodar Valley Corporation (1948) — first multipurpose river valley project |
| **Brahmaputra** | Chemayungdung glacier (near Mansarovar) | **Tsangpo** in Tibet → enters Arunachal as **Siang/Dihang** → joined by Dibang & Lohit → Brahmaputra in Assam → **Jamuna** in Bangladesh. **Majuli** = largest river island. "Sorrow of Assam" |

**Panch Prayag of the Alaknanda** (upstream → downstream): Vishnuprayag (Dhauliganga), Nandprayag (Nandakini), Karnaprayag (Pindar), Rudraprayag (Mandakini), **Devprayag (Bhagirathi — Ganga is born)**.

### Peninsular rivers

| River | Source | Flows into | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Godavari** | Trimbakeshwar (Nashik) | Bay of Bengal | **Longest peninsular river** (~1,465 km); "Dakshin Ganga"/"Vriddha Ganga" |
| Krishna | Mahabaleshwar | Bay of Bengal | Tributaries Tungabhadra, Bhima, Koyna; Nagarjuna Sagar, Srisailam dams |
| Kaveri | Talakaveri, Brahmagiri hills (Kodagu) | Bay of Bengal | Shivanasamudra & Hogenakkal falls; KRS & Mettur dams |
| Mahanadi | Sihawa (Chhattisgarh) | Bay of Bengal | **Hirakud** dam (longest dam of India) |
| **Narmada** | **Amarkantak** (MP) | Arabian Sea | Largest west-flowing river; flows in a **rift valley** between Vindhya & Satpura; Marble Rocks & Dhuandhar falls (Bhedaghat); Sardar Sarovar dam |
| **Tapi** | Multai (Betul, MP) | Arabian Sea | Also a rift-valley river |
| Mahi | MP | Gulf of Khambhat | Crosses the Tropic of Cancer twice |
| Sabarmati | Aravallis | Gulf of Khambhat | Ahmedabad |
| Luni | Aravallis near Ajmer | Rann of Kutch | Inland drainage; saline lower course |
| Sharavathi | Karnataka | Arabian Sea | **Jog Falls** |

> Rule: east-flowing rivers make **deltas**; Narmada and Tapi (west-flowing) make **estuaries**.

### Lakes

| Lake | State/UT | Tag |
|---|---|---|
| **Wular** | J&K | Largest freshwater lake of India (Jhelum) |
| **Chilika** | Odisha | Largest brackish-water coastal lagoon; Irrawaddy dolphins |
| **Sambhar** | Rajasthan | Largest inland saline lake |
| **Loktak** | Manipur | Largest freshwater lake of NE; floating **phumdis**; Keibul Lamjao NP |
| Pulicat | Andhra–Tamil Nadu | 2nd largest lagoon; Sriharikota lies beside it |
| Vembanad | Kerala | Longest lake of India; Kochi on its shore |
| Kolleru | Andhra Pradesh | Freshwater lake between Godavari & Krishna deltas |
| Lonar | Maharashtra | Meteorite-impact crater lake in basalt |
| Pangong Tso | Ladakh | High-altitude brackish lake across India–China LAC |
| Dal | J&K | Srinagar; shikaras & floating gardens |

### Waterfalls and dams

| Waterfall | River / State |
|---|---|
| Kunchikal | Varahi, Karnataka — highest in India |
| Jog (Gersoppa) | Sharavathi, Karnataka |
| Dudhsagar | Mandovi, Goa–Karnataka |
| **Chitrakote** | Indravati, Chhattisgarh — "Niagara of India" |
| Dhuandhar | Narmada, MP |
| Athirappilly | Chalakudy, Kerala |
| Hundru | Subarnarekha, Jharkhand |

| Dam | River | State |
|---|---|---|
| **Tehri** | Bhagirathi | Uttarakhand — highest dam of India |
| **Bhakra** | Sutlej | Himachal (Gobind Sagar reservoir) |
| **Hirakud** | Mahanadi | Odisha — longest dam |
| **Sardar Sarovar** | Narmada | Gujarat |
| Indira Sagar | Narmada | MP |
| Nagarjuna Sagar | Krishna | Telangana–AP |
| Mettur | Kaveri | Tamil Nadu |
| Krishna Raja Sagar | Kaveri | Karnataka |
| Idukki | Periyar | Kerala (arch dam) |
| Farakka Barrage | Ganga | West Bengal |
| Subansiri Lower | Subansiri | Assam–Arunachal (large hydro project) |

lessons.title: Climate, soils and natural vegetation
lessons.body:
### Climate: tropical monsoon

| Season (IMD) | Months | Key points |
|---|---|---|
| Cold weather | Dec–Feb | **Western disturbances** (from the Mediterranean) give winter rain to NW India — good for **rabi wheat** |
| Hot weather | Mar–May | Local storms (below) |
| South-west monsoon | Jun–Sep | Onset over Kerala ~**1 June**; covers India by ~8 July; two branches — Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal |
| Retreating (NE) monsoon | Oct–Dec | **Tamil Nadu (Coromandel) coast gets most of its rain now**; October heat |

**Local winds / storms (hot weather season)**

| Name | Region | Note |
|---|---|---|
| **Loo** | North Indian plains | Hot, dry, dusty afternoon wind |
| **Mango showers** | Kerala & coastal Karnataka | Pre-monsoon; help mangoes ripen |
| **Kal Baisakhi / Nor'westers** | West Bengal, Assam | Violent evening thunderstorms; "tea showers" in Assam; help jute, tea, rice |
| **Cherry blossom / coffee showers** | Karnataka (Kodagu) | Help coffee flowering |

- Highest average rainfall: **Mawsynram** and Sohra (Cherrapunji) on the windward Khasi hills; lowest: western Rajasthan (Jaisalmer) and Leh.
- Windward Western Ghats get heavy rain; the Deccan interior is a **rain-shadow** zone.
- **El Niño** (warm Pacific waters) generally weakens the Indian monsoon; a positive **Indian Ocean Dipole** tends to help it.

### Soils of India (ICAR recognises 8 major groups)

| Soil | Where | Traits | Crops |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Alluvial** | Indo-Gangetic-Brahmaputra plains, deltas | Most widespread; *khadar* = new, *bhangar* = old | Rice, wheat, sugarcane |
| **Black (Regur)** | Deccan trap: Maharashtra, Gujarat, MP | From basalt lava; rich in lime, iron, magnesia, potash; poor in N & P; holds moisture; cracks when dry ("self-ploughing") | **Cotton** ("black cotton soil"), soybean |
| **Red & yellow** | Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Odisha, Chhattisgarh | Red due to **iron oxide**; yellow when hydrated | Millets, pulses, groundnut |
| **Laterite** | Kerala, Karnataka, Goa, Odisha hills, Meghalaya plateau | Formed by **intense leaching** under high rain & heat; acidic | Cashew, tea, coffee; bricks |
| **Arid / desert** | Rajasthan | Sandy, saline; kankar layer | Bajra (with irrigation) |
| **Saline / alkaline** | Dry areas, over-irrigated Punjab-Haryana | Called *usar, reh, kallar*; treated with **gypsum** | — |
| **Peaty / marshy** | Kerala (Kuttanad), Sundarbans | High organic matter | Rice |
| Forest / mountain | Himalaya | Varies with altitude | Tea, fruits |

### Natural vegetation

| Type | Rainfall | Areas | Trees |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tropical evergreen | > 200 cm | Western Ghats, NE hills, A&N | Ebony, mahogany, rosewood |
| **Tropical deciduous (monsoon)** | 70–200 cm | Most widespread | **Teak, sal**, sandalwood |
| Thorn & scrub | < 70 cm | Rajasthan, Gujarat, Deccan interior | Babul, khejri, acacia |
| Montane | Altitude-based | Himalaya, Nilgiris (*shola*) | Oak, deodar, pine, rhododendron |
| **Mangrove (tidal)** | Deltas | **Sundarbans** (sundari tree), Bhitarkanika (Odisha), Pichavaram (TN) | Sundari, rhizophora |

- India State of Forest Report (ISFR) is published every two years by the **Forest Survey of India, Dehradun**. ISFR 2023: forest cover ~21.8% of geographic area; forest + tree cover ~25.2%. Largest forest area: **Madhya Pradesh**; highest % cover: **Mizoram** (ISFR 2023 — still the latest edition as of Sept 2026).

lessons.title: National parks, tiger reserves, biosphere reserves and wetlands
lessons.body:
### Headline facts

| Item | Fact |
|---|---|
| First national park | **Jim Corbett** (Uttarakhand), 1936 as Hailey National Park |
| Project Tiger | 1 April 1973 (9 reserves); run by **NTCA** (statutory, 2006) |
| Tiger reserves | **58** (as of Sept 2026); 58th = **Madhav TR (MP)**, notified March 2025. **MP has the most** (9) |
| Largest tiger reserve | **Nagarjunsagar-Srisailam** (Andhra Pradesh) |
| Largest national park | **Hemis** (Ladakh) — snow leopard |
| Smallest national park | South Button Island (A&N) |
| Project Elephant | 1992 |
| Cheetah reintroduction | **Kuno NP (MP)**, 17 Sept 2022, cheetahs from **Namibia** (then South Africa, 2023); Gandhi Sagar WLS (MP) the second site |
| Biosphere reserves | **18**; first = **Nilgiri (1986)**. **13** are in UNESCO's World Network — Cold Desert (Himachal) added 27 Sept 2025 (as of Sept 2026) |
| Ramsar Convention | Signed 1971 at **Ramsar, Iran**; India a party since 1982. First Indian sites: **Chilika & Keoladeo** (1981) |
| Ramsar sites in India | **101** (as of Aug 2026): 100th = Jai Prakash Narayan Bird Sanctuary (Surha Tal, UP), June 2026; 101st = **Glaw Lake** (Arunachal's first), 3 Aug 2026. **Tamil Nadu** has the most (20); largest = **Sundarban Wetland** (WB); Keoladeo & Loktak are on the **Montreux Record** (threatened) |

### National parks — the animal / feature link

| Park | State | Famous for |
|---|---|---|
| **Kaziranga** | Assam | One-horned rhinoceros; UNESCO site |
| **Manas** | Assam | Tiger + elephant reserve; pygmy hog, golden langur; UNESCO site |
| **Keibul Lamjao** | Manipur | Only **floating** NP (on Loktak phumdis); **Sangai** (brow-antlered deer) |
| **Namdapha** | Arunachal | Four big cats — tiger, leopard, clouded leopard, snow leopard |
| **Gir** | Gujarat | Only natural home of the **Asiatic lion** |
| **Sundarbans** | West Bengal | Royal Bengal tiger in mangroves; UNESCO site |
| **Keoladeo (Bharatpur)** | Rajasthan | Birds (Siberian crane historically); UNESCO site |
| Ranthambore / Sariska | Rajasthan | Tigers |
| Desert NP | Rajasthan | Great Indian Bustard |
| **Kanha** | MP | **Barasingha** (hard-ground swamp deer) — MP state animal |
| Bandhavgarh | MP | High tiger density; historic white tigers |
| **Kuno** | MP | Cheetahs |
| Hemis | Ladakh | Snow leopard |
| Dachigam | J&K | **Hangul** (Kashmir stag) |
| Great Himalayan NP | Himachal | UNESCO site |
| Valley of Flowers / Nanda Devi | Uttarakhand | UNESCO site |
| **Silent Valley** | Kerala | **Lion-tailed macaque** |
| **Eravikulam** | Kerala | **Nilgiri tahr** |
| Periyar | Kerala | Elephants, tigers |
| Bandipur / Nagarhole | Karnataka | Elephants, tigers |
| **Bhitarkanika** | Odisha | **Saltwater crocodile**, mangroves |
| Gahirmatha (marine sanctuary) | Odisha | **Olive Ridley** turtle mass nesting |
| Marine NP, Gulf of Kutch | Gujarat | India's first marine NP (corals) |
| Rann of Kutch Wild Ass Sanctuary | Gujarat | Indian wild ass (khur) |
| Dudhwa | UP | Swamp deer, rhino (reintroduced) |

### Biosphere reserves in the UNESCO network (13)
Nilgiri, Gulf of Mannar, Sundarban, Nanda Devi, Nokrek, Pachmarhi, Similipal, Achanakmar-Amarkantak, Great Nicobar, Agasthyamala, Khangchendzonga, Panna, **Cold Desert** (2025).

> Hook: **Khangchendzonga NP (Sikkim)** is India's only **"mixed"** (natural + cultural) UNESCO World Heritage Site (2016). India has **45** World Heritage Sites — 37 cultural, 7 natural, 1 mixed; latest: Maratha Military Landscapes (2025) and the Ancient Buddhist Site of Sarnath (2026) (as of Sept 2026).

lessons.title: North-East India: geography at a glance
lessons.body:
### The eight states (Seven Sisters + Sikkim, which joined the North Eastern Council in 2002)

| State | Capital | International borders | Geography highlights |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Arunachal Pradesh** | Itanagar | China, Bhutan, Myanmar | Largest NE state by area; Siang (Brahmaputra) enters here; Namdapha, Pakke TRs; Tawang; Kibithu = easternmost point; Sela & Bomdi La passes |
| **Assam** | Dispur | Bhutan, Bangladesh | Brahmaputra & Barak valleys; **Majuli** river island; Kaziranga, Manas; **Digboi** — oldest refinery of Asia still running (1901); largest tea-producing state |
| **Manipur** | Imphal | Myanmar | **Loktak Lake**, **Keibul Lamjao** (Sangai deer); Moreh border town (Asian Highway) |
| **Meghalaya** | Shillong | Bangladesh | Garo-Khasi-Jaintia hills — a detached part of the **peninsular plateau**, separated by the Malda (Garo–Rajmahal) gap |
| **Mizoram** | Aizawl | Myanmar, Bangladesh | **Phawngpui (Blue Mountain)** highest peak; Dampa TR; highest forest-cover % |
| **Nagaland** | Kohima | Myanmar | **Saramati** highest peak; Dzukou valley; Doyang river |
| **Tripura** | Agartala | Bangladesh (on three sides) | Neermahal (lake palace in Rudrasagar lake); Unakoti rock carvings |
| **Sikkim** | Gangtok | China, Nepal, Bhutan | **Kangchenjunga**; Nathu La & Jelep La; Teesta river; Gurudongmar & Tsomgo lakes; first fully **organic** state (2016) |

### Rivers and water bodies
- **Brahmaputra**: enters as Siang/Dihang; joined by **Dibang** and **Lohit** near Sadiya. North-bank tributaries: **Subansiri** (largest), Kameng (Jia Bharali), Manas; south-bank: Burhi Dihing, Dhansiri, Kopili.
- **Barak**: rises in the Manipur hills, flows through Cachar (Assam) and splits into **Surma and Kushiyara** in Bangladesh.
- **Teesta**: lifeline of Sikkim; joins the Brahmaputra (Jamuna) in Bangladesh.

### Connectivity landmarks

| Structure | Fact |
|---|---|
| **Bhupen Hazarika Setu (Dhola–Sadiya)** | Over the **Lohit**; ~9.15 km; opened 2017 |
| **Bogibeel Bridge** | Over the Brahmaputra near Dibrugarh; ~4.94 km — India's longest **rail-cum-road** bridge (2018) |
| Sela Tunnel | Arunachal, on the Tawang road (2024) |
| **Kaladan Multi-Modal Project** | Kolkata → **Sittwe port (Myanmar)** → Kaladan river → Mizoram |
| India–Myanmar–Thailand Trilateral Highway | Moreh (Manipur) → Mae Sot (Thailand) |

### Institutions
- **North Eastern Council (NEC)**: statutory body, 1971; HQ **Shillong**.
- **Ministry of DoNER** (Development of North Eastern Region): department 2001, ministry 2004.
- **Act East Policy** (2014) upgraded the 1991 Look East Policy.

lessons.title: World geography: superlatives, volcanoes, islands, straits and canals
lessons.body:
### Largest / longest / highest

| Category | Answer | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Largest ocean | **Pacific** | Deepest point: **Challenger Deep, Mariana Trench** (~10,900 m) |
| Largest continent / smallest | Asia / Australia | |
| Largest country (area) | **Russia**; then Canada, USA/China, Brazil, Australia, **India 7th** | |
| Smallest country | **Vatican City** | |
| Most populous country | **India** (overtook China in 2023, UN estimate) | |
| Longest river | **Nile** (~6,650 km) | **Amazon** — largest by volume/discharge |
| Longest river of Asia / Europe | **Yangtze** / **Volga** | |
| Highest mountain | **Everest** 8,848.86 m | Longest range: **Andes** |
| Highest waterfall | **Angel Falls, Venezuela** | Victoria Falls (Zambia–Zimbabwe) — largest sheet of falling water |
| Largest desert | Antarctica (cold); **Sahara** (hot) | Driest: **Atacama (Chile)** |
| Largest island | **Greenland** (Denmark) | Australia is a continent, not an island |
| Largest lake | **Caspian Sea** | Largest freshwater by area: **Lake Superior**; deepest & oldest: **Lake Baikal** (Russia) |
| Highest navigable lake | **Titicaca** (Peru–Bolivia) | |
| Lowest land point | **Dead Sea** shore (Jordan–Israel) | |
| Largest coral reef | **Great Barrier Reef** (Australia) | |
| Largest delta | **Ganga–Brahmaputra (Sundarbans)** | |
| Largest bay / largest archipelago | **Bay of Bengal** / **Indonesia** | |
| Largest peninsula | **Arabian** | |
| "Roof of the World" | **Pamir** knot | Highest plateau: Tibet |

### Volcanoes (mostly around the **Pacific Ring of Fire**)

| Volcano | Country |
|---|---|
| Agung, Merapi, Krakatoa, Tambora, Semeru | **Indonesia** (most active volcanoes) |
| Fuji | Japan |
| Pinatubo, Taal, Mayon, Kanlaon | Philippines |
| Mauna Loa, Kilauea | USA (Hawaii) |
| Mount St. Helens | USA (Washington) |
| Popocatépetl | Mexico |
| Cotopaxi | Ecuador |
| **Vesuvius** (buried Pompeii, AD 79), **Etna** (Sicily), **Stromboli** ("Lighthouse of the Mediterranean") | **Italy** — NOT Ring of Fire |
| Eyjafjallajökull (2010 ash cloud) | Iceland (Mid-Atlantic Ridge) |
| **Kilimanjaro** (dormant; Africa's highest) | **Tanzania** |
| Nyiragongo | DR Congo |
| Hunga Tonga–Hunga Ha'apai (2022) | Tonga |
| Erebus | Antarctica |
| **Barren Island** | **India (A&N)** — India's only active volcano; Narcondam is dormant |

### Islands worth remembering

| Island | Country |
|---|---|
| Greenland, New Guinea, Borneo, Madagascar | 1st–4th largest islands |
| Borneo | Shared by Indonesia, Malaysia and Brunei |
| Tasmania, **Lord Howe** (UNESCO) | Australia |
| **Galápagos** (Darwin) | Ecuador |
| **Easter Island** (Moai statues) | Chile |
| Sicily (largest in Mediterranean), Sardinia | Italy |
| Hokkaido, Honshu, Kyushu, Shikoku | Japan |
| Sumatra, Java, Bali | Indonesia |
| Canary Islands / Azores | Spain / Portugal |
| Zanzibar | Tanzania |
| Falklands (Malvinas) | UK (claimed by Argentina) |
| Kuril Islands | Held by Russia, claimed by Japan |
| Hawaii | USA |

### Straits and channels

| Strait | Separates / connects |
|---|---|
| **Palk Strait** | India – Sri Lanka (Bay of Bengal – Palk Bay) |
| **Malacca** | Malay Peninsula – Sumatra; Andaman Sea – South China Sea |
| **Hormuz** | Iran – Oman (Musandam); **Persian Gulf – Gulf of Oman** |
| **Bab-el-Mandeb** | Yemen – Djibouti/Eritrea; **Red Sea – Gulf of Aden** |
| **Gibraltar** | Spain – Morocco; Atlantic – Mediterranean |
| **Bosphorus** | Istanbul; Black Sea – Sea of Marmara (Dardanelles: Marmara – Aegean) |
| **Bering** | Russia – Alaska (USA); Asia – North America |
| **Dover** | England – France (narrowest part of the English Channel) |
| **Magellan** | South American mainland – Tierra del Fuego |
| Sunda | Java – Sumatra |
| Cook | North & South Islands of New Zealand |
| Bass | Australia – Tasmania |
| Torres | Australia – New Guinea |
| Mozambique Channel | Mozambique – Madagascar |
| **Ten Degree Channel** | Andaman – Nicobar |
| **Nine Degree Channel** | Kavaratti group – Minicoy (Lakshadweep) |
| **Eight Degree Channel** | Minicoy (India) – Maldives |
| Duncan Passage | South Andaman – Little Andaman |
| Coco Channel | North Andaman – Coco Islands (Myanmar) |

### Canals
| Canal | Connects | Opened |
|---|---|---|
| **Suez** (Egypt) | Mediterranean – Red Sea | 1869 |
| **Panama** | Atlantic (Caribbean) – Pacific | 1914 |
| **Kiel** (Germany) | North Sea – Baltic | 1895 |

lessons.title: Countries, capitals, currencies and natural resources
lessons.body:
### Neighbourhood and Asia

| Country | Capital | Currency |
|---|---|---|
| Bangladesh | Dhaka | Taka |
| Bhutan | Thimphu | Ngultrum |
| Nepal | Kathmandu | Nepalese rupee |
| Sri Lanka | Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte (legislative); Colombo (commercial) | Sri Lankan rupee |
| Maldives | Malé | Rufiyaa |
| **Myanmar** | **Naypyidaw** | **Kyat** |
| Pakistan | Islamabad | Pakistani rupee |
| Afghanistan | Kabul | Afghani |
| China | Beijing | Renminbi (Yuan) |
| Japan | Tokyo | Yen |
| South Korea | Seoul | Won |
| Indonesia | Jakarta (new capital Nusantara being built) | Rupiah |
| Malaysia | Kuala Lumpur (admin: Putrajaya) | Ringgit |
| Thailand | Bangkok | Baht |
| Vietnam | Hanoi | Dong |
| Cambodia | Phnom Penh | Riel |
| Laos | Vientiane | Kip |
| Philippines | Manila | Peso |
| Mongolia | Ulaanbaatar | Tugrik |
| **Kazakhstan** | **Astana** | Tenge |
| Iran | Tehran | Rial |
| Iraq | Baghdad | Dinar |
| Saudi Arabia | Riyadh | Riyal |
| UAE | Abu Dhabi | Dirham |
| Qatar | Doha | Riyal |
| **Kuwait** | Kuwait City | **Dinar** (highest-valued currency unit) |
| Turkey (Türkiye) | **Ankara** | Lira |

### Rest of the world

| Country | Capital | Currency |
|---|---|---|
| Russia | Moscow | Rouble |
| UK | London | Pound sterling |
| France / Germany / Italy / Spain | Paris / Berlin / Rome / Madrid | Euro |
| Netherlands | Amsterdam (govt seat: The Hague) | Euro |
| **Switzerland** | **Bern** | Swiss franc |
| Poland | Warsaw | Zloty |
| Sweden / Norway / Denmark | Stockholm / Oslo / Copenhagen | Krona / Krone / Krone |
| Ukraine | Kyiv | Hryvnia |
| USA | Washington, D.C. | US dollar |
| **Canada** | **Ottawa** | Canadian dollar |
| Mexico | Mexico City | Peso |
| **Brazil** | **Brasília** | **Real** |
| Argentina | Buenos Aires | Peso |
| Peru | Lima | Sol |
| Venezuela | Caracas | Bolívar |
| Egypt | Cairo | Egyptian pound |
| **South Africa** | Pretoria (executive), Cape Town (legislative), Bloemfontein (judicial) | **Rand** |
| **Nigeria** | **Abuja** | Naira |
| Kenya | Nairobi | Kenyan shilling |
| Ethiopia | Addis Ababa | Birr |
| Ghana | Accra | Cedi |
| **Australia** | **Canberra** | Australian dollar |
| New Zealand | Wellington | NZ dollar |

> Trap capitals: Australia = Canberra (not Sydney), Canada = Ottawa (not Toronto), Brazil = Brasília (not Rio), Turkey = Ankara (not Istanbul), Switzerland = Bern (not Geneva/Zurich), Nigeria = Abuja (not Lagos), Myanmar = Naypyidaw (not Yangon).

### Natural resources — world leaders

| Resource | Leader | Note |
|---|---|---|
| **Proven crude oil reserves** | **Venezuela** (~303 bn barrels), then Saudi Arabia, Iran, Canada, Iraq (OPEC ASB, as of 2025) | Venezuela's oil is heavy (Orinoco belt) — reserves ≠ production |
| Crude oil production | **USA** (largest since 2018; as of 2025) | Then Saudi Arabia / Russia |
| Natural gas reserves | **Russia**, then Iran, Qatar | |
| Coal reserves / production | USA (reserves) / **China** (production; India 2nd) | |
| Iron ore production | **Australia** | |
| Copper production | **Chile** | |
| Gold production | **China** (as of 2024) | |
| Uranium production | **Kazakhstan** | |
| Lithium | Reserves: **Chile**; production: **Australia** | "Lithium triangle": Chile–Argentina–Bolivia |
| Cobalt | **DR Congo** | |
| Bauxite reserves | **Guinea** | |
| Diamonds (volume) | **Russia** | |
| Rare earths | **China** | |

### India's minerals and energy map

| Resource | Key places |
|---|---|
| Coal | Jharkhand (largest reserves: Jharia, Bokaro), Odisha (Talcher), Chhattisgarh (Korba), WB (Raniganj — oldest coalfield) |
| Petroleum | **Digboi** (Assam, oil struck 1889; refinery 1901); **Mumbai High** (offshore, 1974 — largest producing field); Ankleshwar (Gujarat); Barmer (Rajasthan) |
| Largest refinery complex | **Jamnagar** (Gujarat) |
| Iron ore | Odisha, Chhattisgarh (Bailadila), Jharkhand, Karnataka (Kudremukh) |
| Bauxite | Odisha (largest), Jharkhand, Gujarat |
| Mica | Jharkhand (Koderma), Andhra Pradesh (Nellore), Rajasthan |
| Copper | Khetri (Rajasthan), Malanjkhand (MP), Singhbhum (Jharkhand) |
| Gold | **Hutti (Karnataka)**; Kolar Gold Fields closed in 2001 |
| Uranium | **Jaduguda** (Jharkhand), Tummalapalle (AP) |
| Thorium | Monazite sands of Kerala coast |
| Diamond | **Panna** (MP) |
| Lithium | Reserve found at Reasi (J&K), 2023 |

examples.q: Type: 'The Tropic of Cancer does NOT pass through which state?' (options mix border states such as Odisha, Tripura, Jharkhand, Mizoram)
examples.solution:
Recall the fixed west-to-east chain of 8 states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura, Mizoram.
Any option outside this list is the answer — the usual decoys are Odisha, Bihar, Assam, Meghalaya and Manipur.
Answer: the state not in the chain (e.g. Odisha).
examples.shortcut: Draw a line at ~23.5°N on a mental map: it runs just north of Odisha and just south of Assam/Meghalaya — both are outside.

examples.q: Type: 'Strait X connects/separates …' (Hormuz, Malacca, Bab-el-Mandeb, Gibraltar, Palk, Ten Degree Channel)
examples.solution:
Anchor each strait to two land masses first, then the two water bodies.
Hormuz = Iran/Oman → Persian Gulf & Gulf of Oman.
Bab-el-Mandeb = Yemen/Djibouti → Red Sea & Gulf of Aden.
Malacca = Malaysia/Sumatra → Andaman Sea & South China Sea.
Gibraltar = Spain/Morocco → Atlantic & Mediterranean.
For Indian channels count down from north: Ten (Andaman–Nicobar), Nine (Lakshadweep–Minicoy), Eight (Minicoy–Maldives).
examples.shortcut: Degree channels: the bigger the number, the further north (10°N > 9°N > 8°N).

examples.q: Type: 'Which country has the largest proven oil reserves / produces the most oil?'
examples.solution:
Separate reserves from production.
Reserves (in the ground, proven): Venezuela > Saudi Arabia > Iran > Canada > Iraq.
Production (pumped per year): USA leads (as of 2025).
Answer depends on the verb — 'reserve' → Venezuela; 'producer' → USA.
examples.shortcut: V for Venezuela = V for Volume in the ground; U for USA = U for Up-and-pumping.

examples.q: Type: 'Match the national park with the animal it protects' (Kaziranga, Gir, Keibul Lamjao, Dachigam, Eravikulam, Silent Valley)
examples.solution:
Lock the unique pairs first — they eliminate options fastest.
Gir → Asiatic lion (only one place).
Keibul Lamjao → Sangai deer (only floating NP).
Dachigam → Hangul.
Eravikulam → Nilgiri tahr; Silent Valley → lion-tailed macaque.
Kaziranga → one-horned rhino.
Once two pairs are fixed, usually only one option survives.
examples.shortcut: Scan options for one certain pair (e.g. Gir–lion) and strike every option that breaks it.

examples.q: Type: 'Which of these volcanoes is in country X?' (e.g. Taal, Etna, Popocatépetl, Merapi)
examples.solution:
Group volcanoes by country cluster: Indonesia (Agung, Merapi, Krakatoa, Tambora), Philippines (Taal, Pinatubo, Mayon), Italy (Vesuvius, Etna, Stromboli), Japan (Fuji), Mexico (Popocatépetl), Tanzania (Kilimanjaro), USA (Mauna Loa, Kilauea, St. Helens).
Match the stem to the cluster.
examples.shortcut: Spanish/Nahuatl-sounding names → Latin America; Italian → Mediterranean; Bahasa-sounding (Merapi, Semeru) → Indonesia.

traps: Largest proven oil **reserves** = Venezuela, but largest **producer** = USA, and Saudi Arabia is 2nd in reserves. Read the verb before answering.
Highest peak in India = Kangchenjunga (Indian-administered); highest peak **entirely within** India = Nanda Devi; K2 is higher but in PoK — follow the exact wording of the question.

Lakes get swapped: Wular = largest freshwater; Chilika = largest brackish lagoon; Sambhar = largest inland saline; Loktak = largest freshwater lake of the North-East. World: Caspian = largest lake, Superior = largest freshwater, Baikal = deepest.
Tunnels vs passes: Jawahar Tunnel = Banihal pass; Atal Tunnel = Rohtang pass; Zoji La = Srinagar–Leh, not Jammu–Srinagar.
Godavari is the longest peninsular river; Narmada is the largest WEST-flowing river. Narmada and Tapi form estuaries, not deltas — a favourite 'incorrect statement'.
Coastline figure changed: old 7,516.6 km vs re-measured 11,098.81 km (notified 2025). If an option lists 7,516.6 km, it is the older textbook figure — choose based on the year the question refers to.

practice.q: Which river is known as the 'Sorrow of Bihar'?
practice.explanation:
The Kosi frequently shifts its course and floods north Bihar, hence 'Sorrow of Bihar'. Damodar is the 'Sorrow of Bengal'.
Hook: Kosi = Bihar's curse; Damodar = Bengal's.

practice.q: The Palk Strait separates India from
practice.explanation:
Palk Strait lies between Tamil Nadu and northern Sri Lanka; Adam's Bridge (Ram Setu) is at its southern end.
Hook: Palk = path to Lanka.

practice.q: The Tropic of Cancer does NOT pass through which of the following states?
practice.explanation:
The Tropic of Cancer crosses 8 states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram. Odisha lies south of it.
Hook: Gu-Ra-M-Ch-J-W-T-M, west to east.

practice.q: Which is the highest mountain peak located entirely within India?
practice.explanation:
Nanda Devi (7,816 m, Uttarakhand) is the highest peak lying wholly inside India. Kangchenjunga (8,586 m) is higher but sits on the India–Nepal border.
Hook: 'Entirely within' = Nanda Devi; 'in India' = Kangchenjunga.

practice.q: Zoji La pass connects
practice.explanation:
Zoji La links the Kashmir valley (Srinagar) with Ladakh (Leh–Kargil). Jammu–Srinagar is Banihal; Manali–Lahaul is Rohtang; Gangtok–Lhasa is Nathu La.
Hook: Zoji La = gateway to Ladakh.

practice.q: Keibul Lamjao, the world's only floating national park, is located in
practice.explanation:
Keibul Lamjao floats on the phumdis of Loktak Lake, Manipur, and is the last home of the Sangai (brow-antlered deer).
Hook: Loktak → phumdis → floating park → Sangai.

practice.q: Which is the largest freshwater lake in India?
practice.explanation:
Wular Lake in J&K, fed by the Jhelum, is India's largest freshwater lake. Chilika and Pulicat are brackish lagoons; Sambhar is saline.
Hook: Wular = Water fresh; Chilika = Coastal; Sambhar = Salt.

practice.q: Black (regur) soil is most suitable for the cultivation of
practice.explanation:
Black soil, formed from Deccan basalt, retains moisture and is called 'black cotton soil'.
Hook: Regur → cotton belt of Maharashtra–Gujarat.

practice.q: Which of the following is a west-flowing river of peninsular India?
practice.explanation:
Tapi (and Narmada) flow west through rift valleys into the Arabian Sea; Mahanadi, Godavari and Krishna drain into the Bay of Bengal.
Hook: N & T go West (Narmada, Tapi).

practice.q: The Asiatic lion is found in the wild only in
practice.explanation:
Gir forests of Gujarat are the only natural home of the Asiatic lion.
Hook: Gir = Gujarat's lions.

practice.q:
Match the lakes with their states:
A. Sambhar  B. Chilika  C. Vembanad  D. Kolleru
1. Kerala  2. Andhra Pradesh  3. Rajasthan  4. Odisha
practice.explanation:
Sambhar – Rajasthan (saline); Chilika – Odisha (lagoon); Vembanad – Kerala (longest lake); Kolleru – Andhra Pradesh (between Godavari and Krishna deltas).
Hook: Fix Sambhar–Rajasthan first; it eliminates two options.

practice.q: India shares its longest international land border with
practice.explanation:
The India–Bangladesh border is about 4,096 km, touching West Bengal, Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram. China (~3,488 km) is second.
Hook: B for Bangladesh = Biggest border.

practice.q: Which of the following states does NOT share a border with Myanmar?
practice.explanation:
Myanmar borders Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur and Mizoram. Tripura is bounded by Bangladesh on three sides.
Hook: Myanmar's four — A-N-M-M (Arunachal, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram).

practice.q: The Standard Meridian of India (82°30′E) passes near which town?
practice.explanation:
IST is based on 82°30′E, which passes near Mirzapur (Uttar Pradesh). Ujjain was the prime meridian of ancient Indian astronomy — a common distractor.
Hook: M for Meridian, M for Mirzapur.

practice.q: Majuli, one of the largest river islands in the world, lies in which river?
practice.explanation:
Majuli is a river island in the Brahmaputra in Assam, and India's first island district (2016).
Hook: Majuli = Mighty Brahmaputra.

practice.q: The highest peak of South India is
practice.explanation:
Anamudi (2,695 m) in the Anaimalai hills of Kerala is the highest peak south of the Himalaya. Doddabetta is the highest in the Nilgiris; Guru Shikhar in the Aravallis.
Hook: Ana-mudi = 'elephant's forehead', top of the south.

practice.q: Laterite soil is formed mainly due to
options: Leaching under high rainfall and high temperature
practice.explanation:
Heavy rain washes silica and lime out of the soil (leaching), leaving iron and aluminium oxides — laterite. River silt gives alluvial soil; basalt gives black soil; wind gives desert soil.
Hook: Laterite = 'later' what the rain leaves behind.

practice.q: 'Mango showers' refer to
options: Winter rain in Punjab from western disturbances
Retreating-monsoon rain on the Tamil Nadu coast
Pre-monsoon showers in Kerala and coastal Karnataka
practice.explanation:
Mango showers are pre-monsoon (April–May) showers along the Kerala–Karnataka coast that help mangoes ripen. Bengal's thunderstorms are Kal Baisakhi.
Hook: Mango in the south, Kal Baisakhi in the east, Loo in the north.

practice.q: The Tamil Nadu coast receives most of its annual rainfall during
practice.explanation:
The Coromandel coast lies in the rain shadow of the south-west monsoon and gets most rain from the retreating (north-east) monsoon, October–December.
Hook: Tamil Nadu rains when the monsoon returns.

practice.q: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT?
options: The Godavari is the longest river of peninsular India
The Mahanadi drains into the Arabian Sea
The Narmada flows through a rift valley
The Kaveri rises in the Brahmagiri hills of Karnataka
practice.explanation:
The Mahanadi rises at Sihawa (Chhattisgarh) and flows east into the Bay of Bengal, forming a delta in Odisha. The other three statements are correct.
Hook: Only Narmada, Tapi (and small rivers) go west.

practice.q: The Jawahar Tunnel is located below which pass?
practice.explanation:
Jawahar Tunnel (1956) takes the Jammu–Srinagar highway under the Banihal pass in the Pir Panjal range. Atal Tunnel is under Rohtang.
Hook: Jawahar–Jammu–Banihal; Atal–Rohtang.

practice.q: India's first two Ramsar sites, designated in 1981, were
options: Chilika Lake and Keoladeo National Park
Keoladeo National Park and Sambhar Lake
practice.explanation:
Chilika (Odisha) and Keoladeo (Bharatpur, Rajasthan) were India's first Ramsar wetlands (1981). The Convention was signed at Ramsar, Iran, in 1971.
Hook: C & K started the count.

practice.q: The Brahmaputra enters India in Arunachal Pradesh under the name
practice.explanation:
It is the Tsangpo in Tibet, the Siang/Dihang in Arunachal, the Brahmaputra in Assam and the Jamuna in Bangladesh. Lohit is a tributary.
Hook: T-S-B-J — Tibet, Siang, Brahmaputra, Jamuna.

practice.q: Asia's oldest oil refinery still in operation is at
practice.explanation:
Digboi (Assam) refinery started in 1901; oil was struck there in 1889. Jamnagar is the largest refining complex.
Hook: Digboi = Oldest; Jamnagar = Largest.

practice.q: The Ten Degree Channel separates
practice.explanation:
The Ten Degree Channel lies between Little Andaman and Car Nicobar. Nine Degree: Lakshadweep–Minicoy; Eight Degree: Minicoy–Maldives.
Hook: 10 up north (A&N), 9 and 8 down in the Arabian Sea.

practice.q: Which pair of river and dam is INCORRECTLY matched?
practice.explanation:
Tehri Dam is on the Bhagirathi (Uttarakhand); the Sutlej carries the Bhakra Dam.
Hook: Bhakra–Sutlej, Tehri–Bhagirathi.

practice.q: Kanha National Park in Madhya Pradesh is especially known for
practice.explanation:
Kanha saved the hard-ground barasingha from extinction; it is MP's state animal. Rhino – Kaziranga; tahr – Eravikulam; hangul – Dachigam.
Hook: Kanha's crown = barasingha's antlers.

practice.q:
Consider the statements about cheetah reintroduction in India:
1. The first cheetahs were released in Kuno National Park in 2022.
2. The first batch came from Namibia.
Which is/are correct?
practice.explanation:
On 17 September 2022 eight cheetahs from Namibia were released in Kuno NP (MP); a batch from South Africa followed in 2023.
Hook: Kuno + Namibia = 2022 comeback.

practice.q: The Bogibeel Bridge, India's longest rail-cum-road bridge, is built over the
practice.explanation:
Bogibeel (~4.94 km, 2018) spans the Brahmaputra near Dibrugarh, Assam. The Bhupen Hazarika (Dhola–Sadiya) Setu is over the Lohit.
Hook: Bogibeel = Brahmaputra; Dhola–Sadiya = Lohit.

practice.q: The Strait of Hormuz connects the Persian Gulf with the
practice.explanation:
Hormuz lies between Iran and Oman's Musandam peninsula; about a fifth of world oil trade passes through it.
Hook: Hormuz = Oman's door.

practice.q: The Bab-el-Mandeb strait links the Red Sea with the
practice.explanation:
Bab-el-Mandeb ('Gate of Tears') lies between Yemen and Djibouti/Eritrea, joining the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden. The Suez Canal links the Red Sea with the Mediterranean.
Hook: Red Sea — Suez at the top, Bab-el-Mandeb at the bottom.

practice.q: Which is the largest island in the world?
practice.explanation:
Greenland (Denmark) is the largest island; Australia is treated as a continent. New Guinea and Borneo are 2nd and 3rd.
Hook: Green-LAND is the largest land island.

practice.q: Which is the deepest lake in the world?
practice.explanation:
Lake Baikal in Siberia (Russia) is the deepest (~1,640 m) and oldest lake. Caspian is the largest; Superior is the largest freshwater lake by area.
Hook: Baikal = Bottomless.

practice.q: Mount Kilimanjaro, the highest peak in Africa, is located in
practice.explanation:
Kilimanjaro (~5,895 m) is a dormant volcano in north-east Tanzania, close to the Kenyan border.
Hook: Kili-TAN-jaro — Tanzania.

practice.q: Which of the following country–capital–currency combinations is INCORRECT?
practice.explanation:
Myanmar's currency is the kyat; the taka belongs to Bangladesh.
Hook: Taka = Dhaka.

practice.q: Which country has the largest proven natural gas reserves in the world?
practice.explanation:
Russia has the largest proven natural gas reserves, followed by Iran and Qatar.
Hook: Gas order R-I-Q — Russia, Iran, Qatar.

practice.q: Which country is currently the world's largest producer of crude oil?
practice.explanation:
The USA has been the largest crude oil producer since 2018 (shale oil), as of 2025. Venezuela has the largest reserves but low output.
Hook: Reserves = Venezuela; production = USA.
practice.note: Time-sensitive: USA largest producer as of 2025.

practice.q: Angel Falls, the world's highest uninterrupted waterfall, is in
practice.explanation:
Angel Falls (~979 m) is on the Churún river in Venezuela. Victoria Falls is on the Zambia–Zimbabwe border.
Hook: Angel falls from heaven in Venezuela.

practice.q: The Panama Canal connects the
practice.explanation:
The Panama Canal (1914) crosses the Isthmus of Panama between the Atlantic (Caribbean) and the Pacific. Suez joins the Mediterranean and Red Sea; Kiel joins the North Sea and Baltic.
Hook: Panama = Pacific; Suez = Sea-to-Sea in Egypt.

practice.q: Which of the following volcanoes is NOT located on the Pacific 'Ring of Fire'?
practice.explanation:
Etna is in Sicily (Italy), in the Mediterranean, formed by African–Eurasian plate interaction. Fuji (Japan), Pinatubo (Philippines) and St. Helens (USA) ring the Pacific.
Hook: Mediterranean volcanoes (Etna, Vesuvius, Stromboli) are outside the ring.
